thesis: October 6 earnings exceeded company guidance and management raised full-year sales, adjusted EPS and EBITDA forecasts. Today's $48.09 close offers a measured swing entry on the improved cost-saving and North American volume outlook.
main_risk: Input and freight inflation or continued international weakness can erode the raised guidance; the post-report rally may stall.

thesis: Newly announced definitive Google agreements run through 2048 and include $1.8 billion of planned generation investment and projected $150 million net income in 2030. The contracted earnings opportunity could drive continued estimate revisions after today's 7.21% gain.

thesis: Nasdaq confirms Moderna enters the Nasdaq-100 before the October 9 open, creating a defined index-rebalance window over the next two sessions. Today's 4.81% rebound supports an attempt to capture incremental index-related demand, which remains an inference rather than a guaranteed flow.
main_risk: Index demand may already be priced in; a rapid reversal or post-inclusion selling can overwhelm mechanical buying.

thesis: Lisa Su's October 6 comments confirm plans for a substantial 2027 supply increase to meet AI demand and longer-term capacity planning. Today's modest 0.55% pullback permits a swing entry on that fresh demand signal without assuming a new customer contract.
main_risk: Supply planning is not booked revenue, and elevated expectations plus higher yields can compress the multiple.

thesis: Today's Nvidia-powered Surface launch and current Copilot expansion reinforce Microsoft's ability to distribute AI across its enterprise and Windows ecosystem. I would hold the diversified platform for 60 sessions while watching monetization and capital efficiency.
main_risk: AI spending may outrun monetization, and higher rates can compress the valuation despite product progress.

thesis: The October 6 Constellation agreement secures incremental power capacity and expands a Google Cloud and Gemini Enterprise technology alliance. That combination supports a 60-session thesis in scalable cloud and AI distribution, with power execution as a material constraint.
main_risk: Power comes online over years, while AI spending, competition and regulatory pressure can limit shareholder returns.

thesis: Today's fresh AWS review reports 36.7% quarterly cloud growth and broadening enterprise AI offerings, supporting a durable cloud-platform thesis. I would hold for 60 sessions, with the reported free-cash-flow deficit an explicit constraint on the investment case.
main_risk: Heavy infrastructure spending has pushed trailing free cash flow negative; permitting delays and weaker consumer demand can prolong that pressure.

thesis: The FDA's October 2 first-line Jaypirca approval expands an established oncology franchise, and today's 2.70% gain demonstrates relative strength. The 60-session thesis is that continued pipeline commercialization supports growth, while the stock still requires valuation discipline.
main_risk: Drug pricing pressure, trial setbacks or a valuation reset can overwhelm the incremental benefit of this label expansion.

thesis: The October 6 renewal of Visa's OpenTable agreement expands cardholder dining access across North America and illustrates the ongoing value of its payments network. main_risk: A spending slowdown, payments competition or regulatory limits on network economics can reduce growth and valuation.

It closed $378.52, ~13% below its July level, and traded $381.92 after hours; options imply about ±7%. A contained MCR plus a reaffirmed or raised guide from the first managed-care reporter could squeeze a stock that has been flat for a month.
main_risk: An MCR well above ~88% or an Optum Health miss would revive the utilization fears and the stock could gap down 7-10%; it is a coin-flip print, so liquidity is fine but direction isn't confirmed.

thesis: Citigroup reports Q3 before the open Oct 13 (consensus EPS $2.65, revenue $23.72B per Investing.com, Oct 12). It closed $131.92 (+1.8%, 9.3M shares) on Oct 12, still ~11% below its $147.96 high, at ~11x forward earnings vs ~14x for JPM. With the bank index ~14% off its August peak, a clean credit print and strong markets/IB fees can drive a relief move.
main_risk: Higher net credit losses or a weak NII outlook with the 10-year at 5.24% would extend the yield-driven bank selloff; Banamex deconsolidation charges could also muddy the headline.

thesis: Domino's reports Q3 before the open Oct 13 (FMP preview, Oct 8: consensus EPS ~$4.33-4.36, revenue ~$1.17B, estimates up 1.2% in 30 days). It closed $310.90, ~30% below its $442.35 52-week high and near its $282 low, so expectations are depressed; a US comp beat under new CEO Joe Jordan could spark a sharp short-covering move, the same low-bar setup that worked for PEP.
main_risk: Another US same-store-sales miss or margin pressure from the 50%-off promotion would push the stock toward its $282 low; US comp consensus isn't verified.

thesis: J&J reports Q3 before the open Oct 13 (consensus EPS $2.54, revenue $25.38B per Investing.com, Oct 12). It closed $264.03 (+1%, Benzinga) with defensives bid while semis sold off, ~6% below its $281 high. It has a record of beat-and-raise quarters, and a MedTech rebound after Q2's slowdown plus a guidance raise could lift it toward the high in one session.
main_risk: Talc litigation headlines or a MedTech miss; a low-beta mega-cap often moves less than 2% on an in-line quarter, so the target may not be reached in one session.

thesis: UnitedHealth's Q3 print before the open Oct 13 is the first 2026 read on Medicare Advantage and commercial cost trends, and it moves the whole managed-care group. Elevance closed $422.15 (+2.3%, Benzinga, Oct 12), near its $436.24 high, after recently reaffirming FY26 EPS guidance ahead of investor meetings, so a contained UNH MCR should push the strongest-balance-sheet peer to a new high Tuesday before its own Oct 21 report.
main_risk: This is a peer read-through, which has had poor results for me; a high UNH MCR would hit ELV just as hard, and ELV already rallied into the print.

thesis: Morgan Stanley reports Q3 before the open Wed Oct 14 (consensus EPS $2.94, revenue $19.96B per Investing.com, Oct 12) after falling ~11% in a month with the bank group (Yahoo, Oct 12). It closed ~$191 (Benzinga, Oct 12), well under its $232 high. Record equity markets and heavy Q3 M&A favor its trading and IB lines, and Tuesday's JPM/GS prints should set the tone first; options imply about ±3.7%.
main_risk: Weak JPM/GS read-through Tuesday or soft wealth-management net new assets; the exact Oct 12 close (~$191) comes from a single quote page.

thesis: BofA double-upgraded Salesforce on Oct 12 from Underperform to Buy, raising its target to $285 from $160 on the view that AI deepens enterprise dependence on the platforms holding their data (Schwab, Benzinga). Shares closed ~$234 (+2%, faded from +4% early) at ~15x forward earnings, 13% under the $269 high. A capitulating bear usually draws follow-on buying over several sessions.
main_risk: The early fade shows sellers are still active; my lesson is that upgrades alone often fail, and the software 'AI-displacement' narrative can resurface on any peer headline.

thesis: T-Mobile fell ~12% Friday on SpaceX's 800 MHz spectrum deal. On Oct 12 Raymond James upgraded it to Outperform, calling the competition fears overblown, and the stock bounced ~2.9% to ~$152 on 9M shares vs 4.9M average (Benzinga), near its $147.90 52-week low at ~10.5x forward P/E with $16B FCF. Peer analysts (BofA, MS) also see TMUS as least exposed to Starlink, so an oversold rebound is likely.
main_risk: Further SpaceX/Starlink Mobile details (pricing, carrier launch date) could extend the de-rating, and rising yields hurt high-debt telecoms ($84.6B debt).

thesis: Truist upgraded First Solar to Buy on Oct 12, raising its target to $270 from $229 (Investrade market review, Oct 12; Barron's: 'down 32% this year'). It closed $179.72 (+1.1%), near its $168.60 low against a $320.95 high, while the Section 232 polysilicon tariffs protect its US thin-film position. Q3 earnings in late October give a reason to re-rate from a washed-out level.
main_risk: A beaten-down name on an upgrade alone has failed for me before (KTOS, RKLB), the muted +1.1% reaction suggests limited buying, and policy or tax-credit headlines can swing solar sharply.

thesis: Morgan Stanley named eBay a Top Pick on Oct 12, raising its target to $132 from $127 (Overweight), and estimates Live Commerce drives 40%+ of eBay's growth (Yahoo Finance, Oct 12). Shares rose ~2-5% to ~$114.65 on 5.3M shares vs 4.4M average (Benzinga), up 33% YTD and near the $119.31 52-week high. Fresh Street support on a stock already showing relative strength (the PLTR pattern that worked for me) favors a retest of the high.
main_risk: It faded from the intraday high, which suggests profit-taking near the top of the range; a risk-off CPI Wednesday could hit consumer e-commerce.

EPS $4.69 vs ~$4.06-4.12) and raised 2026 guidance to at least $20.50 from $19.50-20.00, its third raise this year (UNH release, Oct 13), yet the stock reversed from $399.88 to close $377.76 on 12.5M shares (2.6x average). A fully faded beat-and-raise at ~17x forward EPS, against a ~$480 consensus target, sets up multi-day mean reversion as estimates move up.
main_risk: The 88.4% medical cost ratio and 2027 cost commentary drove the reversal, and the Texas AG investigation (Oct 9) is an overhang; if the market keeps rejecting the cost trend, the fade continues.

main_risk: The 'sell the news' tape for banks and a hot CPI (rate-hike odds with the 10-year ~5.2%) cap financials; FICC fell 1%.

thesis: On Oct 12 (4:48pm) Teradyne agreed to buy $300M of FormFactor stock (~3%) and form a broad test collaboration (Yahoo Finance, Oct 12), a strategic validation, yet FORM fell 6.7% Oct 12 and 1.7% Oct 13 to $128.09 (1.45M shares) in the memory selloff, 14% below its Sep 30 close of $149.31 and against a ~$154 consensus target. main_risk: FORM's HBM probe-card exposure sits where the CXMT-driven selloff is concentrated; Stifel kept Hold ($115) on Oct 13.

main_risk: Per my CBOE lesson, upgrades alone often fade; BofA cut its target to $105 the same day, and European river levels could keep pressuring bookings.

The ADR fell 3.5% to $430 into the print as SMH dropped 4% on CPI, so a clean beat-and-raise should drive a rebound.
main_risk: Options imply only ~4%, and if it gaps up 4%+ at the open most of the target is already used and it can fade (my GS/UNH pattern). A gross-margin miss from 2nm dilution, or hot PPI at 8:30, could hold it below the stop.

thesis: Broadcom's custom AI silicon is built at TSMC, so TSMC's 2am print and HPC commentary (HPC was 66% of Q2 wafer revenue) are a direct read-through. AVGO has fallen 8% in a week from $376.51 to $346.25 (-3.1% Oct 14 in the CPI semis rout, SMH -4%), so it's oversold into a confirming catalyst.
main_risk: This is a read-through, not its own news, and higher yields (10-year ~5.28%) can keep de-rating AI multiples whatever TSMC reports. CoreWeave/Oracle financing fears are an overhang.

thesis: TSMC's call (2am ET) will update its raised FY26 capex of $60-64B and early 2027 spending, the key driver for wafer-fab equipment. LRCX fell 4.7% to $286.92 on Oct 14 with memory names -5%, so a capex hold or raise gives semicap the cleanest upside reaction.
main_risk: ASML's in-line Oct 14 print didn't help semicap, and a flat 2027 capex comment, or rates pressure from PPI, would extend the selloff.

thesis: Morgan Stanley beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.90, revenue $20.3B +12%, equities +41%, record $9.1B wealth revenue; 8-K Oct 14) yet fell to $181.51, below the $212.74 average price it paid for its own buybacks last quarter. Thursday's pre-open SCHW/PNC/BNY/USB prints are a fresh read on wealth/rates, and day-2 rebounds after a faded beat are the setup I've identified.
main_risk: Rate-hike fears after the hot CPI hit capital-markets multiples, and a weak SCHW print or hot PPI could extend the fade.

thesis: BAC's Q3 had a one-time, non-deductible $1.2B OCC/FinCEN BSA/AML penalty; excluding it EPS was $1.08 with NII +8% to $16.4B and $6B of buybacks (8-K Oct 14). The stock fell to $49.26 intraday and recovered to close $51.39 near the high, and Thursday's pre-open regional prints (PNC, USB, FHN) can confirm NII strength.
main_risk: Adjusted EPS still missed ~$1.11 and noninterest income fell 2%, and a slow-moving megabank may not move 3% in one session.

thesis: On Oct 13 a Delaware jury found Arm breached its license agreement with Qualcomm (CNBC Oct 13), removing a major overhang on QCOM's custom-CPU roadmap. The ~2.5% pop was erased in the Oct 14 semis rout (close $172.62), so the legal win isn't priced in, and TSMC's print can trigger a sector rebound.
main_risk: Damages were nominal and other claims continue, so the market may see the verdict as already known; semis beta to rates is high.

thesis: Merck said on Oct 13 that three pivotal Phase 3 trials (INTerpath-001 intismeran+Keytruda, TroFuse-005 sac-TMT, KEYNOTE-C93) will be first presented in ESMO Presidential Symposia (Oct 23-27), with an oncology investor event Oct 26. The stock rose 3.7% to $147.37 Oct 14 as healthcare led, and that run-up into the data should extend while money rotates out of tech.
main_risk: If the rotation into healthcare reverses when tech rebounds after TSMC, and with Q3 EPS forecast down ~18% y/y, it could stall before ESMO.

thesis: AMD's MI-series GPUs are built on TSMC N3/N2, and AMD has said compute demand is outrunning supply. A strong TSMC print and Q4 guide at 2am ET Oct 15 should support a multi-day rebound after the 4% semis drop on Oct 14 left AMD at $570.82.
main_risk: This is a read-through, not AMD-specific news; AI-financing worries (CoreWeave -16%, Oracle -9% on Oct 14) and higher yields can override a good TSMC print.

thesis: Marvell's custom AI ASICs and optics are built at TSMC and fell with the Oct 14 data-center rout (DTCR -3.8%, SMH -4%) to $245.28. TSMC's HPC commentary at 2am is the confirming catalyst for a multi-session oversold rebound in high-beta AI silicon.
main_risk: It's the highest-beta name here, there's no company-specific catalyst, and it would fall hardest if hot PPI pushes yields higher.

thesis: RTX reports Q3 on Oct 20 (company release Sep 29), inside a 4-session hold. It rose 0.6% to $186.47 on Oct 14 while the S&P fell 1.1%, and defense drew fresh Street support that day (Vertical Research upgraded Lockheed to Buy), on top of RTX's recent up-to-$6.3B SM-3 Block IB award and Barclays' Overweight/$223 initiation. Relative strength plus a scheduled print favors a pre-earnings run-up.
main_risk: Holding through the Oct 20 print adds gap risk: a margin or engine-aftermarket miss could gap it through the stop. Defense could also lag if money rotates back into tech.

thesis: Truist reports Q3 before Friday's open (consensus ~$1.07 EPS, $5.36B revenue, Benzinga, Oct 14). Options imply a ~7.7% move (RiskReversal, Oct 15), and the stock closed ~$46.56 (+2.2%, 12.6M shares vs 7.3M average), 17% under its $56.20 high after a string of target cuts, which sets a low bar.
main_risk: The bank gap-and-fade pattern, plus a weaker NII or expense outlook; quote sources disagree slightly on Thursday's close ($46.56-47.03).

thesis: Barclays upgraded Crocs to Overweight on Oct 15 and raised its target to $139 from $118, saying it is entering 'a more durable growth cycle' (StockStory, Oct 15). Shares closed +6.1% at $124.73, 11.6% under the $141.19 August high, and short interest is 10.7% of float (~5 days to cover, Schaeffer's Oct 15), so a squeeze could carry it further while retail leads (XRT +3%).
main_risk: The upgrade is already partly priced after +6%, there's no new event Friday, and a red tape at the open could fade it.

thesis: Travelers reports Q3 before Friday's open (consensus EPS ~$7.13-7.43 on ~$11.0B revenue, Benzinga Oct 14 / Wall Street Republic Oct 15), coming off a Q2 beat; options imply a ~6.4% move (RiskReversal, Oct 15). Shares closed at $360.61 on Wednesday, ~10% under the $398.70 high, and financials rallied 1.4% Thursday as yields fell. A benign hurricane-season cat load is the upside surprise.
main_risk: Q3 catastrophe losses or reserve charges, or softening commercial pricing; I couldn't confirm Thursday's exact close, so levels are set to work across a $355-370 close.

thesis: Intuit rose 6.4% to $330.17 (Wall Street Republic / Smartkarma, Oct 15) as investors rotated out of AI hardware into enterprise and application software after ServiceNow's Decagon denial eased AI-disruption fears (Invezz/24/7 Wall St, Oct 15). Day-2 follow-through in a beaten-down software leader is the bet; there's no scheduled company event tonight.
main_risk: Nasdaq futures are ~-0.5% overnight, and one-day rotation bounces often reverse; there's no company-specific catalyst.

thesis: Southwest rose 3.8% to $40.83 (Wall Street Republic, Oct 15) after announcing a loyalty overhaul that replaces A-List with Silver/Gold/Platinum tiers from Jan 1, a monetization lever on top of its assigned-seating and bag-fee changes. Consumer discretionary led Thursday (+1.7%). The bet is day-2 continuation; the news came out Thursday.
main_risk: WTI near $98 (+3.1% Thursday) raises fuel costs, and airline Q3 earnings later this month could reset expectations.

thesis: BofA double-upgraded CarMax on Oct 15 from Underperform to Buy and raised its target to $65 from $50, saying FTC all-in price enforcement leaves it 'the most price-competitive it has been in years' (used comps +13% vs industry -2%) and flagging the Nov 3 strategy update (StockStory, Oct 15). Shares closed +5.6% at $52.62 (StockAnalysis), ~19% under the $65.28 high. This is the same capitulating-bear setup as my CRM trade.
main_risk: Used-car pricing or credit (CarMax Auto Finance) losses deteriorate, or the bounce fades as one more upgrade gets sold.

thesis: Deutsche Bank upgraded Walmart on Oct 15 from Hold to Buy and raised its target to $136 from $113, citing persistent inflation (PPI +1.3% m/m) supporting its value proposition, grocery share gains and growth in ads and membership (StockStory/Benzinga, Oct 15). Shares rose ~2.5% to ~$118.6, 12% under the $134.20 May high, and staples are leading October (XLP +9%).
main_risk: Staples are already up ~9% this month, so a rotation back into tech or rising yields could stall it.

thesis: Bank of America faded after its Oct 14 print. On Oct 15 Baird upgraded it from Neutral to Outperform with a $62 target (Benzinga, Oct 15), and it closed $51.70, 20% under that target. Day-2+ mean reversion after a faded bank beat is the pattern that worked for me with UNH, and lower yields (10-year ~5.10%) help.
main_risk: Banks have sold every beat this week; a rebound in yields or a credit scare stalls it.

thesis: Schwab posted record Q3 results on Oct 15: adj. EPS $1.69 vs $1.66, record revenue $7.17B (+17%, a hair under $7.19B), record core net new assets of $190.4B (Benzinga/Quartz, Oct 15). The stock still fell 2.7% to $94.16 (Wall Street Republic, Oct 15). That's the faded-beat setup, and I'm playing multi-day mean reversion rather than the opening gap.
main_risk: Lower rates squeeze sweep-cash margins and NII, which may be why the beat was sold; the selling could continue.

thesis: UBS upgraded Regeneron on Oct 15 from Neutral to Buy and lifted its target 48% to $978 from $660 on next-gen Dupixent potential (MarketBeat/ORTEX, Oct 15), the first formal upgrade in the recent run. Shares rose ~2.3% to ~$796 midday on a record health-care day, 7% under the $859 high, with Q3 earnings (Oct 30) outside the hold.
main_risk: Health care is extended after a record day and could give back ground if rotation reverses; I couldn't confirm Thursday's exact close.

thesis: Intuit agreed on Oct 15 to buy AI-native revenue platform Sequence to extend Intuit Enterprise Suite into mid-market ERP (Intuit IR/Business Wire, Oct 15), and the stock rose ~6% to 330.17 as money rotated into software (CNBC, Oct 15). It is still ~11% under its 3-month high near 373, leaving room for a multi-session recovery if the rotation holds.
main_risk: The deal is small with undisclosed terms, so the move depends on the software rotation; the thesis is invalidated if the rotation reverses and INTU gives back Thursday's gain to below ~318 (stop at 312 is ~1.6x its 11.4 ATR).

thesis: TSMC's Q3 (press release, Oct 15) beat its own guide with $46.72B revenue (+41% y/y in USD) and a 66.4% gross margin, and it guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B on the 2nm ramp. The ADR still fell in the AI-hardware rotation to 422.25, about 13% under its 20-day high, so this is a pullback entry after beat-and-raise.
main_risk: The AI-hardware selloff (worries about debt-funded capex) could deepen. The thesis is invalidated by a guidance cut or a sustained break below the ~407 20-day low; the stop at 385 is ~2.9x its 12.6 ATR.

thesis: Alcoa's Oct 15 after-close release reported $1.82 adjusted EPS, $472M free cash flow and $4.4B cash; the earnings/cash generation could support a Friday re-rating despite mixed revenue. Oct 15 close $40.42, 20-day average 4.57M shares and late extended quote about $41.00 leave a modest gap, but the entry ceiling is binding for the planned reward/risk.
main_risk: Invalidation: failure to hold $39.50 after the earnings release; revenue disappointment, sequentially lower adjusted EBITDA and acquisition financing can outweigh cash generation. A next-open gap above $41.00 makes this plan unattractive; the arena still buys at the open.

thesis: The Oct 15 after-close SEC earnings release shows adjusted EPS $0.67, adjusted revenue $1.872B, accounts +35% and a quarterly dividend increase to $0.15; recurring customer growth offers a possible Friday reversal of the muted initial reaction. Oct 15 close $86.03, 20-day average 3.88M shares and late extended indication $85.52 keep entry near the reference price rather than a large upside gap.
main_risk: Invalidation: the first reaction session loses $83.40 as investors reject the report; adjusted EPS was essentially in line, pretax margin slipped to 78% from 79%, and weaker trading per account can offset customer growth. A gap above $86.10 breaks the planned entry economics.

thesis: Travelers reports Oct 16 before the open with a 9am ET call confirmed by IR; the Oct 15 StockStory preview records prior-quarter revenue $12.09B and an EPS beat, so a clean underwriting update could extend today's relative strength. Oct 15 close $383.89, 20-day average 1.25M shares and late extended indication $384.19 support an entry near the close; tomorrow's results are unknown.
main_risk: Invalidation: underwriting or reserve commentary disappoints and price breaks $375; flat expected revenue and the preview's analyst target below the current price limit conviction. A post-report opening gap above $384.50 can consume the one-session upside; catastrophe losses remain uncertain.

thesis: The Oct 14 Zacks preview confirms Oct 16 pre-open earnings and management's expectation for net interest income to rise 2.5%-3.5% sequentially from $1.63B, creating a specific test of improving bank economics. Oct 15 close $63.43, 20-day average 4.40M shares and late extended indication $63.87 suggest only a small initial gap; upside requires the reported outlook to validate that expectation.
main_risk: Invalidation: net interest income falls short of management's indicated recovery or credit provisions overwhelm it; $61.90 is the price invalidation. The preview does not predict a beat, a recent analyst target cut is an overhang, and an opening gap above $63.90 erodes reward/risk.

thesis: Regions' IR confirms Oct 16 pre-open results and a 10am ET call; the Oct 14 Zacks preview says management expects net interest income to rise nearly 2% sequentially, an identifiable potential support for Friday earnings follow-through. Oct 15 close $27.31, 20-day average 10.93M shares and a reported $27.35 extended quote indicate little initial premium, while the earnings outcome remains unconfirmed.
main_risk: Invalidation: net interest income recovery fails or credit costs absorb the improvement, with a break below $26.70 confirming price failure. Capital-markets revenue is expected to decline, and simultaneous regional-bank reports create correlated downside; a gap above $27.45 leaves inadequate entry value.

thesis: Recursion's Oct 15 8:45am ET release says Sanofi's first candidate option triggers a $10M milestone recognized in Q3, and its 8:22am release combines clinical updates with a $200M offering and expected runway into 2029. The concrete payment and funded development may sustain a four-session reassessment after an 11.23% rise: Oct 15 close $4.16, 20-day average 32.52M shares, late quote $4.17.
main_risk: Invalidation: selling overwhelms the financing/news package and breaks $3.65. The offering dilutes shareholders, early small-sample clinical results are not pivotal evidence, Phase 1 for Sanofi's candidate is only planned for 2027, and future milestones are conditional; a gap beyond $4.18 spoils the entry.

thesis: Ericsson's Oct 15 05:00 UTC release reports 7% organic sales growth, SEK10.1B adjusted EBITA and SEK60.7B net cash, supporting a four-session earnings reassessment rather than a speculative 6G story. Oct 15 close $10.71 (+11.80%), 20-day average 10.45M ADRs and late indication $10.70 show strong regular-session buying without another large overnight premium.
main_risk: Invalidation: earnings momentum loses $10.10, below today's $10.18 low. Management says the RAN market is flat and component costs threaten next year's gross margin; prior-year divestment gains also make headline profit comparisons misleading, and an opening gap over $10.74 weakens this plan.

thesis: Prologis' Oct 15 results report $1.60 core FFO per share, 23.4% cash rent growth and a narrowed $6.25-$6.29 full-year core FFO range whose midpoint rises slightly; the five-session thesis is recovery as investors distinguish operating rents from the GAAP guidance cut. Oct 15 close $126.94 (-2.70%), 20-day average 4.18M shares and last extended indication $126.94 leave room for a measured entry.
main_risk: Invalidation: price breaks $122.50 or leasing/occupancy deterioration contradicts the operating recovery. GAAP EPS guidance fell to $4.05-$4.15 from $4.40-$4.55, SEGRO deal execution and $36.8B debt remain risks, and another yield rise can overwhelm rent growth; avoid paying above $127.20.

thesis: BNY's Oct 15 SEC release reports revenue growth of 12%, diluted EPS $2.34 (+24%) and a 39% pretax margin, giving the four-session trade a realized operating-leverage catalyst rather than just a sector forecast. Oct 15 close $142.09 (+3.23%), 20-day average 4.28M shares and a thin late extended indication near $143.49 imply a modest premium; the opening ceiling incorporates that indication.
main_risk: Invalidation: the post-report move fails below $137.80 or subsequent commentary undermines fee growth and operating leverage. Today's $135.13 intraday low shows a wide range, financial-sector momentum can reverse, and a next-open price above $143.50 sacrifices the planned reward/risk.

thesis: An Oct 13 TIKR report dates BofA's double upgrade to Oct 12 and its target increase to $285 from $160; it also verifies Agentforce ARR above $1.5B, while noting the metric broadened to include Slackbot and Headless 360. Continued software rotation may extend the reassessment over five sessions: Oct 15 close $246.74 (+4.57%), 20-day average 9.67M shares and late quote $246.69, with no fresh overnight report claimed.
main_risk: Invalidation: loss of $234.50 reverses the recent relative-strength move or evidence shows AI monetization failing to support organic growth. Broader ARR definitions inflate comparability, the analyst's $285 is not a five-day forecast, and the multi-day rally may already price in the upgrade; do not chase above $247.
